title: [YouPass Collect] - Renewable energy trends from 1971 to 2011
prompt: The line graph shows the use of renewable energy accounting for total energy from 1971 to 2011. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features and making comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The line graph illustrates the proportion of renewable energy consumption relative to total energy use in six countries over a 40-year period from 1971 to 2011.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, the proportion of energy coming from renewable sources increased in most of the six countries over the period, with the United States showing the most marked growth, while Finland was the only nation to experience noticeable fluctuations. In addition, Finland consistently recorded the highest share of renewables, whereas the United Kingdom relied on them the least throughout the years shown.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at countries with significant growth, in 1971, the United States began with the second-lowest figure at 2.5%, which was half that of Germany's approximately 5% and roughly one-third of France's 8%. The US proportion then rose steadily throughout the entire period, reaching just over 18% by 2011, representing an increase of nearly 16 percentage points. Meanwhile, Germany’s figures initially fluctuated, declining to a low of under 4% in 1987 before recovering dramatically to roughly 13% in the final year. Similarly, France showed a consistent upward trajectory, rising steadily from 8% to around 14.5% over the four decades.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding the remaining countries, Finland started the period with the highest proportion at nearly 25%, significantly above Denmark's approximately 15%, while the United Kingdom recorded the lowest figure at less than 1%. Finland's proportion fluctuated considerably, dropping to a minimum of around 16% in 1988 before recovering to approximately its original level at 23.5% by 2011. Denmark also experienced notable fluctuations throughout the period but showed an overall increase, ending at roughly 17% in 2011. Finally, the United Kingdom demonstrated the slowest but most consistent growth, rising gradually from under 1% to nearly 6% over the four decades, though it remained the lowest among all countries throughout.
